items.title: docs(atlas): classification revalidation cadence — rule-triggered rescans, sampled audits, allowlist expiry (#6051)
items.body: ## What Design record for #6051: `doc/2026-11-09T05-10-38Z_design_atlas_revalidation_cadence.md` — the Atlas classification revalidation cadence under parent #6021. Decides, per the #6051 acceptance criteria (trigger table, scope per trigger, audit method with miss-rate estimate, allowlist lifecycle): - **Triggers (T1–T6)** — recognizer/rule-pack change, new source class or tier-rule change, corpus-growth threshold (≥5% / ≥1,000-chunk run, estimates), quarterly calendar round, allowlist-expiry sweep, incident/ad-hoc signal; priority-ordered with subsumption. - **Scope per trigger per layer** — deterministic + Tier A + pattern pack run full on T1/T4; Tier B NER runs full-internal only when Tier B inputs changed or at most annually, sampled (1,000-chunk pilot shape + 160-chunk secret sample) otherwise; vector-neighborhood and staging checks scoped per trigger. Inherits #6048 run mechanics (run_id, config_hash, 500-chunk batches, idempotent resume). - **Sampled human audit** — every round samples the negatives (300 internal + 160 secret sharing the #6048 calibration draw, estimates) plus a 10% dismissal re-review; rule-of-three/Wilson miss-rate bound tracked round over round, with escalation (catastrophic miss → incomplete round; >2% miss rate → full census; >10% overturn → queue re-opened). - **Allowlist lifecycle** — mandatory reason + expires_at (max 180d) + owner + scoped predicate; T1 suspends affected entries; T5 re-examines un-suppressed before renewal; grandfathering reported per round; no bare recognizer-wide suppressions. - **#6019 plug-in** — staging merge gate, new-class onboarding T2, periodic T4 gate blocking bulk backfills while incomplete, off-peak plan-spend scheduling. - **Dependency honesty** — #6021 has no recurrence recommendation yet; this record assumes the standing-gate branch (parent-program direction) and §8 states the one-off fallback exactly. Forks nothing from #6021; touches #6019 only at the seams; #6049/#6050 untouched siblings. Source note: the prior-art path named in the #6051 body is absent on the fleet laptop; the record is written from the body finding summary + #6021 figures + landed #6048 design and says so, per the task packet. ## Tests Docs-only. `git diff --check` clean. No code tests apply (per packet). Closes #6051 Queue task 13868 (lane opencode, direct). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(atlas-core): gate staging promotion on the mandated embedding model (#7648 M6)
items.body: Implements contract point M6 of the #6060 decision record for issue #7648 (task 14268): the staging-promotion path now asserts the mandated embedding model. - `Registry::promote` in `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/stage.rs` is the merge-on-close transition to `UnitState::Merged`, gated by `assert_unit_embedding_model`: the unit database's recorded `atlas_manifest` `embedding_model` must equal the mandated model (`crate::shards::EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID`, snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0). - A unit recording a different model is refused with an error naming the unit and both model ids, and its state does not change. A unit recording no model is refused as unknown provenance — the same refusal shard discovery applies since M1/M2 (#7646) — so a source whose embedding step ran a non-mandated model cannot be promoted silently; the #6019 ingestion paths inherit the gate by promoting through here. - The recording half of M6 already landed with M1/M2: shard manifests are stamped with the producing model (`embedding_model` key, shards/mod.rs) and the embed pipeline's model is the mandated one by construction (atlas-embed is the snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0 embedder, EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID). - `set_state` is unchanged, so existing staging tests pass unchanged. items.title: docs(atlas): secret-tier local embedder design - no-egress invariant, parity-first selection (#6059)
items.body: Design for #6059 (parent #6019), from queue task 12912 (lane code-w). ## What this decides - **The no-egress invariant, stated as a hard rule:** secret-tier text is embedded locally or not at all. No fallback, retry, batch-discount, or probe route may send it to a hosted embedding API. Routing is by tier tag in one route table whose secret-tier entry has no fallback list; embedder-down means secret-tier ingest queues, never reroutes. - **Model selection, parity first:** candidates are the fleet's current local family (Snowflake Arctic Embed via sentence-transformers, already operational in atlas-search behind the Gate A machinery) and BGE-M3. Selection is by golden-set retrieval parity against the internal tier's hosted model (cross-tier comparability is the property that matters), proposed bar top-10 overlap ≥ 0.8 per source class, ratified with the #6027 sibling; throughput breaks ties. BGE-small is rejected without a track (dormant rollback set, quality gap). - **Fleet-hardware evaluation:** benchmarks run on amd-6 at delta batch shapes (16/64/256 chunks; cold start, tokens/s, p95) — no cloud numbers, no always-on GPU (named dead end, ~$1,080/mo at zero usage). - **Operational home:** a queue-driven batch worker co-located with ingestion on amd-6 — no resident GPU daemon, no new listener; the tier split stays a routing decision, not a second pipeline. - **Failure posture:** queue-and-say-so; a secret-tier #6058 ledger row naming a hosted model is a stop-the-line audit finding. Also names what this design does not decide (internal-tier route, golden-set construction, Gate A tolerance) and the 5-step evaluation checklist for the implementation follow-on. Docs only; no code changes. The doc follows the sibling #6058 cost-ledger design's format. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.body: Closes the Phase 4 audit for #4114 (design #4113). Queue task 6019. ## What this does **Kind-by-gate inventory** — a new section in the `pkgs/id/src/boards.rs` module header doc dispositioning every `BoardObject` variant (all 15, including `GamePost`, which postdates the #4114 variant list) against the design's five gates: 1. Shape (`validate_shape`) 2. References at insert (`validate_links`: existence + board scope, kind where a kind rule exists) 3. Chain / resolution posture 4. Projection effect (`compose_view`, `latest_listings`) under the active-records rule 5. Replication membership + closure (`board_object_set`) Every cell holds, or is a deliberate documented divergence (external content hashes — `Attachment::blob`, `Theme::assets`, `GamePost::package.hash` — are not graph references; `has_role` at insert is existence-based for arrival-order independence; duplicate `(board, revision)` Rules are legal signed history; `Attachment::size_bytes` is unbounded declared metadata no gate depends on). **One finding, fixed here** (small, one variant, per the #4114 acceptance): `resolve_rules` considered every signed `Rules` object, including one superseded through an active `Supersede` record — with the greater content hash in its revision, the superseded text won resolution while `compose_view` hid the same object. Resolution now excludes actively-superseded objects. The frontier computation is shared with `compose_view` via a new `superseded_objects` helper (behaviour-preserving refactor for the view), and a regression test covers the finding: `superseded_rules_are_not_resolved` (two revision-1 rules, the greater-hash one superseded by the lesser-hash one). ## Verification - `rustfmt --check` clean on `boards.rs`. - Local `cargo test` on the laptop did not finish inside the audit shift (the `id` lib-test build exceeded the session budget under shared laptop load; the finding itself is verified by source inspection — the old `resolve_rules` had no supersede filter at all). CI is the test verdict for this PR, including the new regression test and the existing boards suite (36 tests at baseline, incl. the rules-resolution proptest, which is unaffected: it inserts no supersede records). A summary of the audit is also posted on design #4113. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(atlas): ingestion sweep runner core — filter, guardrails, headroom, runbook state (#7969)
items.body: First implementation slice for #7969 (design: doc/2026-11-09T05-12-00Z_design_atlas_ingestion_operations, parent #6019). The issue stays open: live source adapters, staging-shard landing, and the §8(a) Turso verification are the follow-on slice (enqueued as a separate queue task). ## What this PR builds A new `atlas_core::sweep` module plus the `atlas-sweep` operator CLI — the deterministic core of the sweep runner: - **§2 usefulness filter**: the source-class table (boot-records, session-logs, chat-logs, statistics, reports, code-repo) with each class's trigger and question; candidates are accepted / rejected / held with manifest-shaped records `{batch_id, source_class, source_ref, reason_code, bytes, at}` and the closed reason-code set (`no-question`, `duplicate-content`, `oversize`, `secret-tier-held`, `superseded-version`). Evaluation order follows the design: oversize is never partially read, secret-tier items are held (never staged, never sent to a hosted embedder), duplicates reject against the landed content-address set, off-allowlist chat is absence (skip, no record), partial boot segments and unfinished sessions are held for re-offer. - **§4 guardrail monitor**: evaluation over the run's measurement points at the design's initial-slot thresholds — source space low (pause, `guardrail/src-space`) and critical (abort, `guardrail/src-space-critical`), I/O pressure throttle with the `guardrail/src-io` alert on the second consecutive throttled run, staging space (`guardrail/stg-space`), and target write burst (`guardrail/tgt-burst`, pauses the class). No guardrail deletes data, skips the manifest, or promotes a partial batch. - **§5 plan-headroom accounting**: the full report-row shape (run/batch/class, item and byte counts, embedding-ledger reference fields, target usage deltas, envelope percentages, projected days to ceiling, guardrail events, pause state). Alert rules are the design's complete set: 70%-within-180-days projection surfacing, `plan/headroom-80`, `plan/ceiling-stop` at 95% or a ≤30-day projected crossing (pauses the runner's class; resuming is a human decision), and `plan/spend-anomaly` at 2× the trailing median. Envelope quotas and projections are caller-supplied inputs — this code invents no plan numbers (the plan is a human-set constant; #6061 owns the growth model). - **§6 runbook state**: one lock per (source class, host) with `overlap-skip` and stale-lock takeover after 2 h; operator actions `pause-class`, `resume-class`, `run-once`, `dead-letter list|retry|drop` (3 failure strikes across runs dead-letters an item), and `report --run|--cycle` over persisted report rows. Landing is idempotent by content address; the runner never promotes (the #6057 gate's job) and never deletes. ## Not in this PR (follow-on) Live discovery adapters per class, landing into the staging shard via `stage.rs`, the #6058 ledger-row reference at embed time, host measurement probes, and §8(a) — verifying the live Turso usage fields for read/write deltas before §5 percentages are relied on. **No schedule is created or enabled** (Drew-gated on #7969). ## Tests - 8 new unit tests: filter order + closed reason set, the per-class design table, guardrail thresholds (each rule), the headroom alert set, run-once end-to-end (records, counts, report row, duplicate on re-run), pause/overlap/dead-letter behavior, ceiling-stop pausing the class, lock staleness takeover. - Full `cargo test -p atlas-core`: all suites pass (137 lib tests + integration suites). - CLI smoke-tested: `pause-class`/`resume-class`, `run-once` over a JSON request (sparse candidate objects accepted via serde defaults), `report --run` returns the persisted row. Task 20051, lane any-l. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) to 7.30.1 and updates ancestor dependencies [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici), [cf](https://github.com/cloudflare/cf/tree/HEAD/packages/cli) and [wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/wrangler). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

    Breaking: cf dns records batch is now cf dns records bulk-apply. There is no compatibility alias; update scripts to use the new command name.

  • aa1d296: Use worker.name from cloudflare.config.ts when --worker is omitted

    The API-backed cf workers commands (secrets, versions, deployments, get and delete) now fall back to the project's worker.name, evaluated with the current --mode, when --worker is not passed. The name's source is printed on stderr unless --quiet is set; destructive confirmations still name the resolved Worker. Config load and validation errors are reported when the fallback is needed. Passing --worker works as before.

Patch Changes

  • a3eb61e: Accurately report missing auth profiles

    When commands resolve or are given a non-existent auth profile, report that the specified profile was not found and list available profiles instead of emitting a misleading "No authentication token found" error.

    Use Wrangler's shared SQL splitter so cf d1 migrations apply <database-id> --local can apply migration files larger than SQLite's per-statement SQL length limit when their individual statements fit. Keep each migration and its bookkeeping insert in one atomic batch, preserving rollback on failure.

    Read piped secret values and prompt for missing required fields during dry runs, just as during execution. Reject missing required body input instead of showing an incomplete successful preview, while continuing to redact secrets and skip authentication and API requests.

Minor Changes

  • #16961 bf7568a Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Show configured trigger targets during experimental wrangler triggers deploy --dry-run

    Dry runs now print a "Would deploy" summary of routes, custom domains, cron schedules, Queue producers and consumers, Workflows, event triggers, and Email Routing addresses instead of exiting without a summary. Explicitly empty cron schedules and Email Routing addresses are shown as removals. The preview makes no API requests or authentication checks; when workers.dev is enabled, it reports that setting without looking up the account's subdomain.

  • #16679 be6aa81 Thanks @​mglewis! - Add images.url_transformations to the Wrangler configuration

    The images block now accepts a url_transformations object for controlling /cdn-cgi/image/ transformations on requests served by a Worker. enabled is required, and allowed_origins optionally lists the origins images may be fetched from (use ["*"] to allow any origin). binding is now optional, so url_transformations can be configured without an Images binding:

    {
  "images": {
    "url_transformations": {
      "enabled": true,
      "allowed_origins": ["images.example.com"]
    }
  }
}

    Like the rest of the images block, url_transformations is not inherited by named environments, and must be specified in each environment that needs it.

    cloudflare.config.ts gains the equivalent setting as a top-level images field on the Worker, with the Images binding remaining in env:

    export default defineConfig({
  worker: {
    name: "my-worker",
    compatibilityDate: "2026-11-01",
    images: {
      urlTransformations: {
        enabled: true,
        allowedOrigins: ["images.example.com"],
      },
    },
  },
});

    cf migrate carries images.url_transformations over to this field.

    This change adds configuration and validation only. url_transformations is not supported in previews.

  • #14114 dce615c Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Add --show-diff flag to wrangler triggers deploy

    When --show-diff is passed, the command fetches the currently deployed trigger configuration from the remote worker and displays a colored diff against the local configuration before deploying. This covers routes, custom domains, cron schedules, and the workers_dev/preview_urls subdomain settings. Route and custom-domain lists are fetched only when that category has local entries to deploy, avoiding unnecessary permission requirements. Queue consumers and event triggers are not compared.

    The flag also works with --dry-run to preview these changes without actually deploying. Displaying a diff requires authentication, including during a dry run.
